title: Felix and the Bakery
premise: Rafael Montrose, a jaded wedding planner, is stranded by a snowstorm in the small town of Bellhaven with Odette Lark, his rival planner and the woman he loved and lost ten years ago. Forced to share quarters above Felix's Bakery — run by Felix, an elderly baker who once employed them both as teenagers — they must collaborate on one final wedding: Felix's own, scheduled for New Year's Eve, before his failing heart gives out. As they plan the ceremony that taught them everything about love, Rafael and Odette finally speak the apology each has rehearsed for a decade. The wedding happens just in time; Felix dies peacefully weeks later, leaving them the bakery and, at last, permission to begin again.
about_author: Mara Blackwood is the pen name of a former pastry chef who spent five years working in wedding-season kitchens before turning to fiction full-time. She writes love stories set in warm rooms during cold weather, believing that forgiveness, like bread, requires patience and heat.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Forgets
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He orchestrates a flawless society wedding while privately believing love is a trainable muscle — contain it, and it won't fail you. A call from Bellhaven: Felix, the baker who mentored him at nineteen, is getting married and wants Rafael to plan it. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Contract
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. She accepts the same commission, stunned to learn her rival was hired too — and that Felix did it deliberately. Driving toward Bellhaven, she rehearses the speech she's written in ten unsent letters. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. A freak snowstorm closes the mountain road; Rafael and Odette arrive hours apart and find the only lodging is the apartment above Felix's Bakery, one bed, two egos. They agree to a truce until the roads clear. Emotional beat: forced proximity, old wounds humming.

chapters.title: What Felix Baked at Midnight
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Woken by the smell of cardamom buns, he finds Felix baking at 3 a.m., teaching him the groom's cake recipe as if passing down scripture. Felix asks pointed questions about Odette that Rafael deflects. Emotional beat: tenderness disarming defensiveness.

chapters.title: The Guest List of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Planning sessions force her and Rafael through every decision couples make; each choice detonates a memory of their own aborted engagement a decade ago. She discovers he kept the ring box. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as anger.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rehearsed Sentences
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A power outage traps them by candlelight; the argument they've avoided for a decade finally erupts — why she left, why he never followed. Both say half their rehearsed sentences and storm to separate corners. Emotional beat: catharsis interrupted, tension at its peak.

chapters.title: Felix Collapses
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Felix collapses mid-bake; roads still snowed in, hospital forty miles away. In the terrifying quiet of waiting, Rafael admits to Odette that he stopped believing in weddings because losing her proved love could be survived but not lived. Emotional beat: fear stripping pretense away.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. At Felix's bedside, she finally says her sentence — the full apology, the reason she ran — and Rafael answers with his. They weep, laugh, and choose each other not as a return but as something new. Emotional beat: release, the story's emotional climax.

chapters.title: A Wedding in the Snow
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Roads clear enough for guests; they stage Felix's wedding in the bakery itself, flour-dusted and candlelit, every detail an act of love rather than logistics. Rafael plans it believing again; Odette reads a blessing she wrote for herself years ago. Emotional beat: joy earned through wreckage.

chapters.title: The Recipe He Left Behind
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. Felix has died peacefully; his will leaves them the bakery and a letter: 'You were my best mistake.' Rafael and Odette reopen Felix and the Bakery together, first batch in the oven, hands entwined. Emotional beat: belonging found, identity remade, memory honored.
